Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.gov_ph OILG NO. S 20 LIL HON. MA. ISABEL L. SAGARBARRIA Vice Mayor City of Dumaguete Dear Vice Mayor Sagarbarria: This has reference to your letter dated January 19, 2024, requesting this Department's opinion regarding the Annual Investment Program (AIP) of Dumaguete City for the Calendar Year 2024. Culled in your letter are the following pertinent factual antecedents: • • • • The plans constituting the proposed 2024 AIP were completely submitted to the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) only on November 8, 2023. It was only in October and November 2023 when the SP received, partially and then in full, the proposed 2024 AIP that it was able to start performing its duty to review the voluminous documents appurtenant thereto. After a series of committee meetings, the SP found the need to make recommendations to the CDC [City Development Council] on certain items in the proposed AIP. On December 19, 2023, the SP, during its Regular Session, adopted the Consolidated Committee Report of the Committee on Finance and Appropriation and passed Resolution No. 411, series of 2023. The Resolution invited the attention of the CDC to the recommendations of the SP and requested its appropriate action. Instead of convening the CDC to consider the recommendations of the SP, the LCE, on his own initiative, returned the subject AIP to the SP and, in a letter dated January II, 2024, insisted that the same be approved without any modifications. Premised from the foregoing, arose the following issues for this Department's opinion, thus: 1. Whether or not it is within the prerogative of the SP under the Local Government Code and DILG issuances to refer back to the CDC the Summary of AIP and CDC Full Council Resolution No. 2023-37 and seek appropriate action on the accompanying SP recommendations as stated in SP Resolution No. 411 , Series of 2023. 2. Whether or not the Mayor has the right not to convene the CDC (Full Council) and, by his own act, deny the recommendations. What are the legal repercussions if the Mayor does not convene the CDC to tackle the recommendations? What are the legal remedies? Can he be ordered by the DILG? "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

3. In case the Mayor, as Chairman, does not convene the CDC, can the majority of the members of the CDC (Full Council), on their own, convene and pass the necessary resolution, returning the proposed AIP to the Sangguniang Panlungsod with their response to the SP's recommendations? At the outset, attention is respectfully directed to pertinent provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 (hereinafter referred to as the Code), thus: Section 305. Fundamental Principles. - The financial affairs, transactions, and operations of local government units shall be governed by the following fundamental principles: (g) Local governments shall formulate sound financial plans, and local budgets shall be based on functions, activities, and projects, in terms of expected results; (h) Local budget plans and goals shall, as far as practicable, be harmonized with national development plans, goals, and strategies in order to optimize the utilization of resources and to avoid duplication in the use of fiscal and physical resources; (i) Local budgets shall operationalize approved local development plans; (j) Local government units shall ensure that their respective budgets incorporate the requirements of their component units and provide for equitable allocation of resources among these component units; (k) National planning shall be based on local planning to ensure that the needs and aspirations of the people as articulated by the local government units in their respective local development plans are considered in the formulation of budgets of national line agencies or offices; (l) Fiscal responsibility shall be shared by all those exercising authority over the financial affairs, transactions, and operations of the local government units; and (m) The local government unit shall endeavor to have a balanced budget in each fiscal year of operation." Section 455. Chief Executive. Powers, Duties and Compensation "(a) The city mayor, as chief executive of the city government, shall exercise such powers and perform such duties and functions as provided by this Code and other laws. (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the city mayor shall: (1) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the city government. and in this connection, shall: (i) Determine the guidelines of city policies and be responsible to the sangguniang panlungsod for the program of government; (ii) Direct the formulation of the city development plan, with the assistance of the city development council, and upon approval thereof by the sanqqunianq panlunqsod, implement the same. xxx." (Emphasis ours) Section 109. Functions of Local Development Councils. - "(a) The provincial, city, and municipal development councils shall exercise the following functions. (1) Formulate long-term, medium-term, and annual socio-economic development plans and policies; (2) Formulate the medium-term and annual public investment programs; (3) Appraise and prioritize socio-economic development programs and projects; (4) Formulate local investment incentives to promote the inflow and direction of private investment capital; (5) Coordinate, monitor, and evaluate the implementation of development programs and projects; and (6) Perform such other functions as may be provided by law or component authority." (Emphasis ours) Section 114 provides: "Section 114. Relation of Local Development Councils to the Sanggunian and the Regional Development Council. - (a) The policies, programs, and projects proposed by local development councils shall be submitted to the sanggunian concerned for appropriate action. (b) The approved development plans of provinces, highly-urbanized cities, and independent component cities shall be submitted to the regional development council, which shall be integrated into the regional development plan for submission to the National Economic and Development Authority, in accordance with existing laws." (Emphasis ours) Having laid down the foregoing, it may be well to note that central to the fiscal affairs of the local government units (LGUs) are the complementary roles of the Office of the Local Chief Executive (LCE) and the sanggunian under the Code and other relevant laws. Section 305 of the Code enunciates the fundamental principles that guide LGUs vis-å-vis their financial affairs, transactions, and operations. Under the Code, the office of the LCE has the primary responsibility for the formulation of fiscal plans, such as the Annual Investment Program (AIP) and the Comprehensive Development Plan (CDP). Parenthetically, Section 109 of the Code mandates the Local Development Council (LDC), which is chaired by the LCE, to formulate the AIP. Now, while it is the LCE who is primarily mandated for the formulation of the AIP, the sanggunian is not precluded from making recommendations and subsequently referring back the AIP to the office of the LCE for the latter's consideration, as it deems necessary. In the present case, may we note that we are not furnished with a copy of the subject Resolution. Be that as it may, pursuant to Section 114 of the Code, the sanggunian is mandated to take appropriate action on the AIP prepared and submitted to it by the Page 3 of 4

LDC. To our mind, the phrase "appropriate action" by the sanggunian includes making recommendations to the LCD and not just the approval of the AIP. Along this line, it is to be emphasized that the Code clothed the sanggunian with the power to pass resolutions to convey their sentiments on matters including those related to fiscal plans, such as the AIP. The collaboration or interplay between the office of the LCE and the sanggunian is pivotal in formulating policies, plans, and programs that are responsive to the needs and priorities of their constituents. Accordingly, this Department is of the view that it is well within the prerogative of the sanggunian to make recommendations on AIP prepared and submitted by the office of the LCE. As to the second issue, we shall address it along with the third issue since they are interrelated. It is established that the sanggunian concerned shall act on the AIP formulated by the LDC and subsequently submitted by the LCE to the sanggunian as provided for under Section 114 of the Code. Now, it is well to note that the Code does not expressly mandate the LCE to convene the LCD as the only means or sole mechanism for addressing the action undertaken by the sanggunian. Be that as it may, it behooves the LCE to act on the recommendations or proposals made by the sanggunian to the AIP. Assuming arguendo that the LCE does not act on the recommendations put forth by the sanggunian, without justifiable reason, the sanggunian may resort to administrative remedies under Section 60 of the Code. Along this line, it is to be noted that it is not proper for the members of the CDC to singly, or on their own, convene or pass any resolution without the presence of the mayor, who is the chairperson of the council, let alone without his approval thereto. Finally, it is to be emphasized that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government, and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare invalid or illegal any legislative measures enacted or passed by local government officials, nor does it have authority to declare invalid or illegal any acts committed by local government officials that are alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code or any other applicable laws. The same must be threshed out in the proper forum. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, Unde OUSEL cc: uthority of the Secre ry: AN VICTOR R.
